On a Mac, deleting CodePress and installing it again, then opening it signed out, now runs the first-run onboarding from Welcome even though the old app data is still there. An in-app update, moving the app, or a signed-in reinstall does not.

Ghostty tabs show inline images from the Kitty graphics protocol (`kitten icat`), keep them through scrolling, reattach and window reload, and follow the pointer shape apps set with OSC 22. The Ghostty engine moves to upstream 6fba0873 on Zig 0.17. Pilot Ghostty tabs opened before this update reopen once as a fresh shell in the same folder, with their agent resumed.
A synced project's artifacts can now be listed and read from its home Mac over the pane relay, the same path its Files use, so another machine can show them once its view lands.
Ghostty tabs get a working ⌘F: the find bar searches the whole scrollback, scrolls to and highlights matches, and shows "n of m" in the main window, the popout and the quick terminal pane.
On a Mac, onboarding's git row offers Install, which opens Apple's Command Line Tools dialog, and then says to finish in Apple's window and Check again.

Ghostty tabs on phones now support touch selection: a long press selects a word, drag handles extend the selection in either direction, and the touch Copy and Paste bar works on it. Copied text has wrapped lines joined. A quick swipe still scrolls and a tap still opens the keyboard.
Terminal can now create a session on another connected computer, one of yours or a teammate's shared with you, for the computer picker coming next.

Ghostty tabs now have clickable links. Hovering an OSC 8 link, URL or file path underlines the whole link, even across wrapped rows, and shows the pointer cursor. ⌘-click or Ctrl-click opens it, following the Cmd+Click to Open setting, and the right-click menu shows the link and file items.

The headless Linux CLI's bundled Node now searches its own directory for libraries too (RUNPATH `$ORIGIN:$ORIGIN/../lib`), so a teammate's runtime copy stages with its libatomic and their Orchestrator and tabs start on a shared Linux server.
Stamp the stored section cache through its own build define, so web deploys stop renaming about 100 shared chunks. Terminal's cache behavior is unchanged.
A headless Terminal (`codepress-terminal serve`) now starts, reads and takes messages for a teammate's project on a shared computer, instead of refusing it as `orchestrator_authorization_refused`.
Make provider logos readable in dark mode on brand tiles and on Account → Orchestrator's model pickers.

Synced copies and cloud-run projects now have an Artifacts tab: a copy lists what its home Mac's Orchestrator and workers published, a cloud project what its Orchestrator and workers uploaded. While the home can't answer, the tab says why ("Connecting to…", "… is offline", "Update CodePress Terminal on …").

First run in the desktop app now asks everyone to sign in to CodePress right after Welcome, with Continue locally in the footer, and the two answers lead to different screens. Signed in: set up your workspace, connect your accounts, the permission steps, then Start a project. Continue locally: connect your AI and GitHub on this Mac, the permission steps without the remote-access ones, then Let's Go. The Connect step puts pull-request setup first, moves Gemini, Grok and Muse into an Other connections dialog, and says Codex instead of ChatGPT. Every middle step's button reads Continue.

The Artifacts gallery and viewer now use the app's theme colours instead of bright blue, in light and dark. The active filter chip matches the rail's selected tab, and an HTML artifact with no background of its own now shows dark text on white in dark mode.

An Orchestrator or reclaimed worker now keeps going when its provider CLI updates itself. Its next process runs the new version at the same path and resumes the same conversation, instead of stopping with "The provider runtime changed while sign-in was starting". If the CLI is removed, the session stops with a message naming the CLI and path, and a CLI that changes during a first start now says to start again rather than mentioning sign-in.

The live browser now follows a sign-in window when a site opens one, returns to the page that opened it when it closes, stays connected if the window vanishes, and comes back to the same window after a dropped connection. The handoff browser launches with FedCM off, because its dialog cannot be seen or answered in the live view, so sites use their popup or redirect instead.

Onboarding's four Mac permission screens are now one, "Let agents use this Mac", with an Agents group and, when signed in, a Reach this Mac group. Review permissions and What changed open the same screen.

Runs on → Shared with you now lists the computers shared with every teammate, including teammates who haven't turned on running cloud agents on their own computers. When the list can't be read, Runs on keeps the last list and says "Couldn't check shared computers. Retrying…" instead of quietly dropping the group.

The Terminal tab's list has a computer selector: pick This computer, one of your Remote Access computers, or one shared with you. The list shows only that computer's sessions, picking an unconnected computer connects it, and "+" opens a new session on it. The rail's machine picker is the same selection.

A teammate's Runs on start, project reads and messages now work on a shared computer whose Terminal just restarted: the relay frame carries their actor grant, which Terminal checks (their own, for this computer, not expired, never for someone whose access ended) before starting their Orchestrator host.
Ghostty tabs render in popout windows, and keep the scrollback depth from your Scrollback setting instead of the native worker's 1000 lines.

Focus rings now appear only after keyboard input. Closing a menu, popover or select with the mouse leaves its trigger focused without a ring; Tab, the arrow keys, Enter, Space and Escape still show it.
Ghostty tabs now match xterm on mouse-wheel distance, row height and row count, and send one CR per line break in a bracketed paste.
Processes now opens from its own Activity icon in the rail, directly above the machine button, instead of a row in the machine menu. On phone it is a row at the top of the Machine sheet.

Upgrading no longer leaves a Ghostty tab's old shell and agent running beside the new ones. Re-admission now ends the old process itself and only starts the new shell once it is gone; otherwise the tab stays on its old owner.

Closing a Ghostty tab now releases its connections right away, so a long session can no longer use up the terminal's connection limit and block new tabs of any kind. Each computer now has room for about 120 Ghostty tabs on two windows. If you pass that limit, the tab you open says so and your other tabs keep working.

Claude and Codex workers, local Orchestrators, kickoffs and sign-ins on a computer with no compatible `claude` or `codex` installed now run the native CLI Terminal already ships, and handing a worker to such a computer no longer fails as unavailable. A compatible CLI you installed yourself still comes first. The _Automatically set up connected providers_ setting is gone: setup is always on, a saved value is ignored, and older windows or agents that still send it get a success with a note that it was removed.
Repair the broker upgrade QA scenarios for the current launcher layout. QA tooling only; the app does not change.

Added an Artifacts section to the rail, with search, person, date and type filters over your organization's artifacts. It replaces the Apps page's Agent artifacts view; an old link to that view opens the new section.

Typing `claude` or `codex` in any Terminal tab now works on a computer with neither installed: it runs the copy Terminal ships. Workers and the Orchestrator find them the same way. Terminal's copies are last on PATH, so a `claude` or `codex` you install yourself always runs instead, even when your `~/.zshrc` rebuilds PATH. Settings → AI Agents → Accounts says "Using the built-in Codex 0.165.0" (or Claude Code) while the built-in copy is the one in use.

Teammates' runtime now stages on a headless Linux CLI (`codepress-terminal serve`). Staging failed every attempt with "cli/claude: No such file or directory", because the CLI keeps `node_modules` beside `server-dist/`; Terminal now points the shared-computer helper at a view joining the two. No helper update or "Prepare again" is needed.

The Orchestrator Hand off dialog shows the step tracker (stopped → starting → running) from the real hand-off states, waits for a running turn and then hands off by itself instead of asking you to try again, and on reopen shows a start that is still under way or one that failed, with Try again on that Mac or Hand off to the cloud. After a failed start it says the project is assigned to that Mac, which hasn't started it, rather than still on the old one, and at 800×600 the list never shows a group heading without its first row.

Set up GitHub: with no GitHub CLI on this computer, the GitHub row in onboarding and in Settings → AI Agents installs a pinned `gh` (2.103.3, checked against GitHub's published SHA-256), signs it in through GitHub's device flow with the code shown in the row, and runs `gh auth setup-git` so `git push` to github.com uses that login. A `gh` already signed in is left alone. Workers and the Orchestrator find the installed `gh` through Terminal's managed command folder. Windows keeps the cli.github.com link.

GitHub through your CodePress account: signed in, the GitHub row in onboarding's Connect step and Settings → AI Agents writes your account's own GitHub login into gh (installing Terminal's gh first if needed), so gh and git work with no separate GitHub sign-in. A gh already signed in to github.com is never touched. An account with no GitHub login gets Link GitHub; anything else falls back to Set up GitHub with the reason, and "Use a separate gh login" stays on offer.
Cloud chat tells you to open the web app when an agent asks for a secret.

Connect your accounts: signed in, onboarding's Link Claude and Link Codex sign in, then link the account to your CodePress account as a Personal account in the same press, so your other computers and cloud agents can use it. Accounts already linked show as linked with no press on a second computer. If linking fails the account still works on this computer, with Retry link; a workspace that doesn't sync AI accounts keeps them on this Mac and says so. Gemini, Grok and Muse stay in Other connections, on this computer only.

A computer the backend puts on the edge relay now serves its same device URL through the relay: Terminal attaches to the relay, serves each request against its own local server with every existing sign-in and network-access check, and leaves its tunnel up as the fallback, which the URL uses whenever the relay is unreachable. Nothing changes while the relay is off for the computer. Settings shows one diagnostics line under Tunnel Diagnostics while the relay is assigned.
Move Computer → Agents → Accounts to Account → Agent accounts. There is now one account page, and it opens signed out too.

Ghostty tabs now survive fast output. Running `yes` or `cat bigfile` no longer freezes the tab behind the attach banner: the terminal slows the program down instead of losing output, Ctrl+C works during the burst, and other tabs keep updating. A tab whose rendering worker restarts now recovers on its own.

Onboarding's Connect step and the signed-out Agent accounts page now use today's names: a Personal account needing reconnect points to Settings → Account → Agent accounts, and the signed-out hint says "Sign in to connect provider accounts for CodePress agent sessions."
The Ghostty Terminal Engine setting moved from Settings → Agents to Settings → CodePress app, beside the other terminal rendering settings. It works the same way and your saved choice is kept.
Agent account rows keep the account's name on a narrow window, and a phone-sized Remove dialog's Close is easier to reach.
With collections on, file artifacts in collections beside Apps, from a collection's Add picker or an artifact's card.

A native PTY broker now stops on SIGTERM with a bash tab open instead of hanging and then spinning at 100% CPU. It no longer treats a tab as Terminal's own process because a path in its arguments contains `codepress-terminal`.

A teammate's window on a shared computer keeps showing their own agent count instead of falling to "Agents unavailable", and no longer offers "Activate Software Factory" or the owner's update and restart pills.
Shared-computer windows now use your own keyboard shortcuts, including prefix mode.

Starting a project from a teammate's window on a shared computer: a repository you type now reaches your Orchestrator, and the window says folders on that computer aren't available. Disabled repository and folder pickers now stay closed.
An idle Orchestrator now keeps its provider process for a full idle window after its last turn or release, instead of being released again a minute or two after a short wake.
A teammate's `gh` on a shared computer now works outside a clone when the command names the repository, and otherwise says exactly what to do. A failed clone or push says why too.

Reclaim Idle Agents no longer quits a worker with a background agent or shell running, or a finished result it has not received yet, at the idle window or under critical memory pressure. If a quit does open Claude Code's "Background work is running" panel, Terminal closes it with Esc instead of leaving the worker frozen behind it, never presses Enter on it, and tells the Orchestrator if Esc doesn't work.
Size selected CI unit-test shard counts by measured file weight while retaining full-run capacity.

A tab Terminal can't write to now says so instead of looking like an agent waiting. It shows a notice with what to do, `list_tabs` and diagnostics report it, a worker's Orchestrator hears once per incident, and reclaim sweeps stop trying to quit it.
Ghostty tabs keep the history depth your Scrollback setting asks for through a reload, and a steady stream no longer makes a tab reload its history.
The Orchestrator rail now takes a list of launching rows, and a launch can show that it failed to start. Terminal still shows one launch at a time, so nothing changes yet.

Onboarding's signed-in Connect step shows a Claude or Codex account that is already a Personal account as "Linked", never offering Link: it reads the Personal listing fresh, shows "Checking…" or "Couldn't check your CodePress account · Retry" until it knows, and the daemon no longer answers the listing from a poll made before the current sign-in.

A local Orchestrator's plan issue now reaches its shared plan page, so signed-in teammates see the link there. It is sent after the parent issue is linked and after every plan publish; an older backend only logs a warning.

Check the bundled Claude and Codex CLIs when Terminal and the Orchestrator host start, and remember what was found, so the first Orchestrator or worker launch no longer waits several seconds to find a CLI.
Send this computer's hardware binding when it registers with CodePress, so the account picker lists each computer once instead of once per old device id.

Agent accounts: the computer picker's trigger now reads "Accounts on" before the computer's name on every width, and only the name truncates. The picker is now the shared `@codepress/ui` component so the web can use the same one.

Your Orchestrator and its Claude and Codex workers can now use stored secrets without ever seeing them. When one is missing or needs a new host, a card in the Dock asks you, and the value goes straight to CodePress.

A new launch opens on the tab that holds it: sending an Orchestrator project from Chats switches the rail to Projects, and sending a chat from Projects switches it to Chats, where its starting row reads "New chat". A starting row no longer shows on a list that won't hold it.

Signing out no longer leaves Terminal with no service when the old background daemon takes more than 20 seconds to stop. Sign-out keeps watching it for up to a minute, then finishes removing the service and starts window 1's own daemon, so signing back in works without relaunching the app.
A local Orchestrator working in a repository with a design kit is told where the kit is when it opens, and composes its mockups from it instead of copying tokens by hand.
Artifact cards that group a project's pages now have Share, Copy link and Open canvas. Share opens the plan page's own link, worded for all of its pages, on the web app's address.

A broker from before the SIGTERM fix can again be replaced in place. The new shutdown deadline was required when reading its state, so replacing it was refused and a second broker was started instead.

Agent accounts is now first under Settings → Account, and the "Which account each computer uses" block at the bottom of the page is gone: the "Accounts on" picker above the accounts chooses each computer's account. A long "Running on <computer>" label now stays inside its account card.
Codex workers keep their MCP servers and both trust folders however long their paths are: the launch's command now rides in a private file instead of the typed line.

An open chat that becomes an Orchestrator project now turns into the project view in place: the status header, the Work and Plans tabs, and the row moving from Chats to Projects in the feed, without a reload and keeping any typed draft. The thread shows the "This chat is now a project" line as one quiet record.

A local chat that is about to change a git repository now becomes an Orchestrator project in the same conversation (`become_project`), with its history kept and the build already started on your request, so the pull request it opens is tracked on a work item.

New chat in the Orchestrator now always opens a fresh composer, even while an earlier start is still waiting for its computer. Each launch keeps its own row in the list until its project appears. If a start fails, its row stays with the reason, and you can retry it, edit the brief, or dismiss it. Launches are kept across a reload.

Pasting or typing what looks like an API key into an Orchestrator thread now warns you before it's sent, and you can save it as a secret instead. There's also a lock button in the composer to add a secret at any time.

Reorder the left rail: drag a section icon to a new place (the others slide aside and an empty slot opens where it lands) or right-click it for Move up, Move down and Reset rail order. The order is saved to your account and shared by every Terminal and the web.
Send this data folder's fingerprint (`folder_binding`) when Terminal registers with CodePress, and retry a slow hardware id read once before falling back to a random device id.

A collection can have one share link, team only or public, drawn on one canvas. A public link shows only items that are already public on their own, and the Share dialog names what it leaves out and why.

A local chat that opens a pull request without first becoming a project is now promoted to one when that turn ends, and the pull request goes on a work item, so it is never left untracked in the chat.

Settings and the setup guide now use a Terminal-styled slider for Font Size, Scroll Speed and the Code Editor font size: a slim accent-filled track, the toggle's white knob and an editable value field, replacing the macOS system slider and number spinner.

A merged PR's "Could not verify" entries are now only the worker's unverified behaviours: the attribution footer and Merge safety lines end the section, sub-bullets fold into their lead, and worker briefs define Could not verify and offer an optional Notes section that is never copied into the landing.

Runs on → Auto honors a saved machine order: it stays on the first ranked computer that can run the work and is under the busy limit (85% by default), and ranks by load only when every ranked computer is busy or unavailable. With no order saved, Auto is unchanged. Agents can read and set the order with `get/update_terminal_agent_settings` (`autoMachineOrder`).

A landing with a draft now keeps the Orchestrator's own sorted "Could not verify" list, and the landed card counts only that list. Each merged pull request's raw list stays on the record behind "As the pull requests reported it".

Answering the Orchestrator's "Land without it" now lets the Orchestrator land the project with its own summary: the platform's "Land the project" card stays hidden while the Orchestrator's turn is queued or running, and a stale card pressed on another device is refused instead of landing.
Handing off a cloud project's Orchestrator to a Mac no longer stops at "Stop these workers first": its live workers move to the Mac with it, and the Hand off dialog says so.

Settings → My computers has an Auto order: rank your computers for Runs on → Auto by dragging or with the up and down buttons, add or remove them, and choose when a computer counts as busy (85% by default). Each computer shows its live usage, which one is over the limit and which one Auto would pick now. The order saves to your account, so it applies on every computer and on the web.
The empty Orchestrator kickoff now greets you like Chat does: the coloured "Hello, {name}!" with "What should the Orchestrator get done?" under it.

A Terminal whose data folder comes back under a new device id sends that folder's fingerprint when it asks which URL it serves, so it gets its old URL and nickname back even before the device has registered.
Local Orchestrators offer, once per project, to set up a design kit in a repository that has none when the organization turns on the "Design kit setup offer" feature flag.

Under critical memory pressure, Terminal now freezes an idle worker that still has background work running instead of leaving it to use memory, on Linux and macOS. The worker thaws by itself when pressure clears, after 8 minutes, on a message, viewer or keystroke, or on the next start, and keeps its terminal and its work. macOS tabs stopped under pressure used to stay stopped; they now thaw the same way. `get_terminal_diagnostics` reports `agent_freeze`. A worker whose turn has ended no longer counts as holding a dialog, so with Terminal's hooks installed it can now be reclaimed when idle.

A window opened over the edge relay and left alone no longer sends anything on a timer, so the computer's relay can sleep. Updates, cards included, arrive by push over the window's one socket, and everything else is read when needed: on first use, on a push, on reconnect, and on return to visible. Local windows, tunnel windows and older daemons keep today's polling and heartbeat.

Hand off… on a cloud project's Orchestrator picks its destination from tiles: your Macs, then Cloud last. A Mac that can't take it stays dimmed and says why when it's focused, and while it moves the chosen tile shows a ring with the step it's on and a Steps list.

A tab's hand-off notices (moved, recovery after a failed hand-off, and set-aside transcript lines) now share one banner: a ✓, ! or ring mark, a title, a detail line and actions on the right, drawn in your theme's colours instead of a fixed red or amber card.

Hand off this session, a cloud session's Hand off… and the Agent tab's cloud chat strip now use the same destination tiles, step ring and outcome as the Orchestrator's picker: your Macs first and Cloud last, with asleep or unavailable Macs dimmed and their reason shown on focus. A cancelled handoff now offers Start a new handoff.

Team chats: Preferences gains "New chats are visible to" (Organization default, Team or Personal) and "Share past chats…", and the feed rail offers a one-time "Share your past chats with the team?" card. All of it shows only while the organization's Team chats flag is on.
Orchestrator posts can now be marked retracted, and every thread read, restart, search and project move treats a retracted post as not there. Nothing sets the mark yet.

Hand off for an Orchestrator project now picks its destination from tiles (where it runs now, your other Macs, then Cloud), dims a destination that can't take it with the reason under the grid, keeps the preview behind Details, and shows the move as a ring with timed Steps and a ✓ or ! outcome.

Local Chats can move to another of your Macs through the Orchestrator handoff, and come back with Continue here. Each one arrives with its Claude or Codex conversation and its folder's uncommitted work. A Mac whose Terminal can't take a chat yet is listed as needing an update.
No user-visible change: two source comments no longer name the removed `apps/deck` app.
Local Chats can be handed off to another Mac: Hand off… is on a chat's rail row ⋯, its header ⋯ and another Mac's chat row, and opens the move picker with chat wording.

Capacity hosts now record which VM driver they run (`kata-qemu`, the default and only driver today). `host join --driver` refuses an unknown or reserved driver before installing anything, `host status` shows the driver, and the host reports its real OS and driver to the backend. Linux hosts behave as before.

A Local Chat can now continue in the cloud. Its Claude or Codex conversation and its folder's code go with it, and the chat on this Mac reads "Runs in the cloud" with Open chat. A chat with no GitHub repository, or with a repository the organization hasn't connected, can't be sent and shows why. If the cloud refuses to start it, for example at the agent limit, the chat stays here with Retry and Resume here.

Opening a teammate's Team chat in the cloud chat view shows who owns it and that it is read-only, with Add to my feed, Continue in my own chat, Send to… and an "Ask your agent about this chat" box that starts your own chat with it attached.

Orchestrator workers no longer wait for hours while macOS reports memory pressure `warning` with plenty of memory free: at `warning` a launch goes while free memory stays at or above max(25% of RAM, 8 GB). `critical`, Linux and small Macs are unchanged.

A message you sent the Orchestrator mid-turn can be taken back while it waits. On a project running on this machine, each queued message has Edit, which returns its words, files and mentions to the box, and Delete, which removes it and offers Undo. If the Orchestrator read it first you see "Too late", and a message already handed to Codex says it can't be changed.

Moving an Orchestrator project no longer fails with "The prepared project worker set changed" when a live worker renamed its branch: the move records the branch the worker is really on, and a branch that changes again mid-move is refused with a message naming the worker.
Your own automations can run on your Mac in the sandbox: "Run my automations on this Mac" walks you through setting it up.
The feed rail gets a My feed / Team switch, a People filter, owner avatars on Team chats, a Following section in My feed and a lock on Personal chats, when the organization has team chats on.

A worker launch held for memory headroom now shows why, how long and in what place it waits on its work item, refreshed each minute, and wakes the Orchestrator after 30 minutes (then every 2 hours) with the reason and the machine's largest processes. `project_snapshot.machine.launch_queue` reports the project's queued launches.

A window opened over the edge relay now stays quiet on every screen, including the Orchestrator: worker activity arrives as a push, and other reads happen when a surface opens, on reconnect and on return to visible, instead of on a timer.

Your Mac runs only automations you allowed there: Terminal asks once per automation, signs that with the Mac's key, and refuses any order it didn't allow, including replayed or expired ones. Editing an allowed automation never asks again.

Claude tabs now see one `codepress-computer-use` MCP server on every Mac and window instead of a hashed entry per window, so Claude's cached tool list survives a move. Terminal removes its old per-window entries from `~/.claude.json` and pooled tab configs, leaving any entry it did not write.

Session handoff now resumes Claude and Codex with the source tab's model, effort, MCP config, settings, system prompt and permission flags, so the destination keeps the provider's prompt cache. Older receivers get the unchanged handoff.

Edit and Delete on a queued message now work from a synced copy, on another Mac or on the web. A message its home hasn't picked up yet is taken back straight away, even while that home sleeps. One it has picked up goes back through the home: if the home is away you see "Can't reach" and the message stays, and if the Orchestrator read it first you see "Too late". A home on an older version shows no buttons.

A headless machine can now see and act on an unconfirmed key: `codepress-terminal status` says so, and `codepress-terminal confirm` emails its owner a link. Terminal also signs a computer's access change, which had been going out unsigned. It now also signs its reads of another machine's tab files (the Artifacts tab's list and content), which the backend requires in organizations that enforce drive proof.
A Terminal → cloud handoff now sends the session's last model (and Codex effort), so the cloud continues on the same model.

Handoff status now reports whether the destination's first resumed turn kept the prompt cache (`cacheOutcome`, with `priorCoverage` as the pass line), and `scripts/handoff-cache-report.ts` prints prior coverage and the cache-read share around each handoff in a transcript.

Mac chats now start with the visibility the composer chose. With Team chats on, Terminal's new-chat composer shows the Team | Personal chip. A chat started from the web on this Mac also keeps the web chip's choice, and the chat's synced copy is created with it.

`codepress-terminal host join` now works on Apple-silicon Macs as a CI-only capacity host. It runs as the console user under a LaunchAgent and keeps its own `TART_HOME`. It fetches a short-lived host token from the backend and long-polls the CI scheduler, then runs each GitHub Actions runner in a single-use Tart VM behind the pf guest firewall. Doctor, status, drain and leave cover the Mac. Linux hosts are unchanged.

A Local Chat with no GitHub repository (no folder, a plain folder, or a checkout whose origin isn't GitHub) can now be handed off to the cloud when your organization's cloud supports it. Only the conversation goes and continues in an empty cloud workspace; the move dialog says the folder's files stay on this Mac. Chats in a GitHub checkout move exactly as before.

Handoffs keep the source's subscription account: a handed-off Claude tab, Orchestrator worker or Orchestrator starts on the same account at the destination when it is connected there and not limited, so the first turn can read the prompt cache.

This Mac's own enforcement (the local-client gate, consent, request signing and the Stop all work switch) now turns on when the organization has Automations on Macs on, not only Local-first routing. A backend that predates the new flag answers as before.

The local Orchestrator's system prompt no longer names this machine's paths, browser server or MCP connections, so it stays byte-identical when a project or chat moves to another Mac and the provider's prompt cache still applies. A "Where you run" message carries those values instead: on a conversation's first turn, and again as "Where you run (updated)" after a move or when they change. After the provider compacts the conversation, the next turn sends the message again.

Publishing an automation now first lists what changed without proof since it was last published (code, secrets by name, schedule, triggers), in orgs where machine work is on. You confirm the list before the publish vouches for it, or cancel.

Team chats: a teammate's Mac chat in the Team feed (or Following) now opens read-only from its cloud copy, with the owner and machine chips, when it last synced, Add to my feed, Send to…, Continue in my own chat and the Ask box. If the owner makes it Personal, it says it is no longer shared. The owner of a synced Mac chat can switch it between Team and Personal from the chat's ⋯ menu.
Settings → My computers shows whether each of your Macs runs your automations: ready, needs setup and why, or off. It appears only where Automations on your Macs is turned on for the organization.

Hand off → This Mac moves directly when the home Mac is awake but slow to answer: an online home gets a second, longer probe, the press reuses the preview's direct answer, and a takeover with nothing synced asks the home once more before refusing.

Where the organization keeps cloud copies, a Local Chat now uploads its snapshot and conversation like a project, a new Synced project or chat uploads a snapshot as soon as it is created, and a Synced project with no snapshot in the cloud gets one at launch or wake, so any of them can be picked up while this Mac sleeps.
The device channel proves this computer's key when the backend asks for it, so a copied sign-in can't pose as your Mac or receive its work.

Project handoffs no longer get stuck when a worker changes folders inside its own checkout during the move. The handoff checks that each worker is still in the checkout it recorded instead of the exact folder, so a cancelled move can release its workers again.
Record who owns every Terminal setting (follows you, this device, or set on the computer), ahead of preferences following you to other computers. Nothing visible changes.

Org owners and admins can add the Mac they're using to the team runner pool from Settings → Computers, with no command line or root password. The Mac joins as a CI-only computer: you choose macOS and Linux ARM VMs and their slots, see whether the images fit on disk, and acknowledge that it becomes a team CI machine. The row then shows each step, from enrolling and building images to approval. The pool list now names each computer's OS and what it runs, so agent capacity and CI capacity are easy to tell apart.

Switching the Orchestrator feed from My feed to Team draws rows at once: Team is read ahead once after My feed loads, and a Team list kept from an earlier session is shown dimmed until the live list arrives.
Quitting Terminal while a project or chat is being switched to Synced no longer reads its record after the record has closed, which logged errors on the way out.

The Team feed's Filter menu now offers Repository, Started from, Agent and Runs on (Cloud, Mac, Cloud VM) beside People, each counted over the Team chats you can read and narrowing cloud and Mac chats alike.

An agent tab now hands off in any state. A tab that never ran a turn, whose transcript doesn't appear within 10 seconds, or that runs Kimi moves with its folder and opens the same agent fresh on the other Mac. Text typed but not sent, all of its lines, arrives in the destination's prompt unsubmitted, once the agent there is ready for it. A tab whose shell is gone moves as stopped. Continue here resumes a copy saved mid-turn from its last whole line, and continues a copy that has no transcript as a fresh session.

Hand off → This Mac now picks up a Local Chat whose home Mac is asleep from its cloud copy: the chat opens here with its conversation, in this Mac's checkout of its repository (or its own folder), and continues the same conversation.
A new chat's waiting line now says "Starting a chat…" (or "Starting a chat in the cloud…" / "Starting a chat on <machine>…") instead of "Starting the Orchestrator…" or "Starting the agent…".

Project handoff no longer refuses because of what a worker is doing. A worker waiting on a prompt or holding unsent input moves and is told so on arrival (its prompt is asked again there, never approved for it). A worker mid-launch is waited out. One whose agent exited, has no terminal or no transcript moves as stopped, with its worktree checkpointed, and starts fresh on its branch at the destination. A failed worker's leftover process is stopped first, and an in-flight worker message is waited out briefly.

Orchestrator projects can be shared with your team: the New project form has the Team/Personal chip, a teammate's Team project opens read-only with its Work drawer, and the owner switches it from the project menu (behind team chats).

A teammate's leased Claude or Codex subscription on a shared computer is renewed when it rotates, asking CodePress for a new token, and never more than once a minute: renewing early no longer loops until the computer's lease budget runs out.
Any member of an organization with Self-hosted runners on can add the Mac they're using to the runner pool for CI from Settings → Computers. It takes no work until an owner or admin approves it.
Claude and Codex agents now switch to another account at a usage limit by default. Turning it off for a provider in Settings → Agent accounts keeps it off; Kimi stays opt-in.

The kickoff composer no longer caps files at 20 MB. It holds each dropped file and uploads it at Send by the transport of the place the project starts: Cloud takes files up to 200 MB through S3, and This machine up to 32 MB inline. A file too large for the place you picked is refused at Send with that place's limit, keeping the draft and its files, and a reload names any large file to attach again.

Your font, shortcuts, scrolling, bell, cmd-click, GitHub Actions display, quick keys and editor appearance now follow your account to every computer, phone and browser you sign in on. A remote window no longer writes them to the computer it is looking at.
Fix Codex Orchestrator startup when a project's MCP transport conflicts with a generated connection.

An account pick refused because CodePress is rate-limiting this computer's leases now says so and when to try again, in Settings and in the remote "Accounts on <computer>" view. A saved choice refused by a lease 429 or 503 retries by itself (no sooner than Retry-After), and a choice skipped because the account needed reconnecting applies once it is reconnected.
Read a QA report posted by someone with write access to the repository as the pull request's QA verdict, so the Orchestrator no longer reports "no QA" on a pull request a person inherited.

An agent tab that never ran a turn can now be handed off to Cloud. It opens there as a new cloud chat on the tab's repository and code, and any text typed but not sent becomes that chat's first message. Before, such a tab could only go to a Mac.

A teammate's Team project now has the Ask box ("Ask your agent about this project"), Continue in my own chat and Send to…, as a teammate's chat does; past projects you started yourself can be shared through "Share your past chats and projects"; and making a shared project or chat Local only now tells the cloud, so it leaves the Team feed (behind team chats).
A link to a page inside an App now opens that page in Terminal, instead of being treated as the App's page already on screen.

A Synced chat whose home Mac stopped mid-write can now be picked up on this Mac instead of being refused. When the cloud copy of its conversation ends in an unfinished record, the chat's agent starts again from the chat's synced messages, and the arrival note says its own conversation could not be restored.

A local Orchestrator on Claude now keeps its prompt cache for an hour on any account, so a turn after a long wait reads its context from cache instead of writing it again. Before, this needed a Claude subscription that was not in overage. Your own `CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL` still wins, and `CODEPRESS_PM_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=5m` turns it off.

Settings now says whose each setting is. The General tab groups its rows under Your preferences, This device and Set on this computer, and the other tabs say whose they are. A window on another computer names that computer in a banner and marks what is set there.
The font-size slider in the setup guide and Settings is marked so automated layout checks skip its track and knob, which sit on top of each other by design. Nothing changes on screen.

Answering a question from another computer no longer leaves the composer or the next question locked. The card lets go once the home applies the answer, or when the question opens again (a revised plan), without switching chats. While the answer is still on its way, words you type send as an ordinary message.

Terminal now reads the organization's new "CPU and thermal admission" flag, on desktop and on headless machines, and `get_terminal_diagnostics` reports it as `cpu_thermal_admission`. Nothing obeys the flag yet.

From a teammate's Team chat, start your own chat or Orchestrator project with the full New chat composer docked under the thread: Runs on, model and folder are yours. The chat starts where Runs on says (this Mac included), and its first message shows the teammate's chat as a chip. The agent gets that chat's recent posts. A chat that is no longer shared is refused before anything starts, and your draft is kept (behind team chats).
Report CPU and thermal pressure, and an estimate of sustainable cores, in diagnostics, capacity status and Orchestrator snapshots. This only reports; nothing is held or capped.

A computer's Claude and Codex accounts always have one active when one can be. The first account you add is selected for you, and removing, pausing or restricting the active account moves to the next one (the account CodePress lists as yours, else the oldest Local account). A new computer with no default account starts on your oldest Personal account. Terminal still never replaces a CLI login you made yourself or overrides a mode you chose, and never picks a Team account. An account moved to Personal stays active and is reported to CodePress, so the web shows it selected.
Stop the reported sustainable cores falling while the machine has not tried running within the figure, so work that was already running cannot slide it to the floor.

HTML artifacts of any size open in the Artifacts viewer instead of showing "Too large to preview". CSV, JSON, Markdown, code and text files keep the 2 MB preview limit, and gallery cards for HTML over 2 MB keep a static tile.
A teammate's window on a shared computer now uses that teammate's own font, scrolling and other followed preferences, not just their shortcuts, and never the owner's.

Land a Plan-ready project by hand: "Land project…" now appears for a project whose plan is ready but was never built. Landing it cancels the queued work items, retires the Orchestrator and closes the plan issue, and the dialog says nothing ships.

Account pages in Settings are the full width of the pane again. The line saying whose the settings are had pushed them in by 32px on each side, which narrowed Agent accounts and the Orchestrator page.
A project's home can now show its land preview and land the project when its owner asks from a synced copy, through the same land sequence as the home's own Land.

A usage-limit wait now ends as soon as an account the run may use is free: switching the active account to one that is not limited, or turning automatic switching on while one is connected, resumes waiting Orchestrator turns and scheduled worker relaunches within 30 seconds instead of at the reset.

Relayed windows: say 1009 when a message is too large, stop reconnecting after a second one, and keep a relay connection whose large frame is still sending. Terminal now reports relay protocol 2, which is what the backend requires before it assigns the relay.

A teammate's message to a chat or Orchestrator project on this Mac now reaches its agent. It arrives in the inbox labelled as from a teammate, or from a teammate's agent, and shows in the thread as "Teammate · From <name>". It never answers an ask or approves a plan. A paused project keeps the message until you resume it, and a message sent while this Mac was offline arrives once it reconnects (behind team chats).
The Orchestrator now calls your computers machines ("this machine", "your other machines") instead of Macs, since CodePress runs on Mac and Linux.
A chat moved to the cloud keeps its name, its visibility and the thread you saw, and the move shows as one line.

Start my own Orchestrator project with Runs on set to Cloud now works from a teammate's Team chat: the cloud project's first message shows their chat as a chip, and its Orchestrator reads that chat's recent posts. Starting from a teammate's chat on another of your Macs that needs an update now says to update CodePress Terminal there. When a start is retried while the chat is being unshared, the retry replays the project the first attempt made instead of being refused (behind team chats).
A teammate on a shared computer can now open Settings and see their own preferences and what the computer's owner set, read-only and naming the owner.
A teammate's cloud-hosted Orchestrator project on the Team feed opens read-only in Terminal, with its Work panel, and you can start your own chat or project from it (behind team chats).
With the CPU-aware admission flag on, a hot machine paces or holds new worker launches with a clear reason, and the capacity broker grants only what the machine can sustain.

A window on the edge relay no longer loses its quiet state to one transient failure: a stream the daemon refused for a moment goes back to the window's socket, and the project rail's 15 s read is bounded while a stream is stalled and stops while hidden.

Land project… on another Mac's project: the ⋯ menu of a building or Plan-ready project homed on another Mac or a Cloud VM now lists Land project…, reads the preview live from the home and lands it there. An asleep home says so and offers Try again; nothing is queued.

The shared Orchestrator screens (Hand off picker, feed rail, Continue on menu, kickoff notes) say "this machine", "your other machines" and "Local machine" instead of "Mac". A handoff label of "This Mac" from an older Terminal still reads as this machine.

With the CPU and thermal admission flag on, limit running workers' CPU while the machine is hot and restore it automatically as it cools: a worker CPU quota on Linux and background QoS on macOS. The cap state appears in capacity status and diagnostics.

Projects and chats on this computer now take files up to 2 GB, 4 GB per message, at kickoff and in the thread. A file streams to Terminal instead of travelling as base64, so a long screen recording no longer costs memory. A refusal at Send clears once you change the files. A file too large to move with a project is named in the handoff, and the rest of the project's folder still moves.
Settings and the terminal font show what this device last knew straight away, then update when the network answers.

Orchestrators and chats on this machine can now coordinate with a teammate's agent. list_team_chats finds the Team chats you can read, and message_team_chat sends the agent behind one a message, labelled as from your agent. A teammate's agent can reply the same way, and its reply arrives in your inbox. An Orchestrator owned by another person now reads as teammates_orchestrator, naming that person (behind team chats).

Under a teammate's Team chat or Mac chat, Send can now message the owner's agent ("Message <owner>'s agent") as well as start your own chat or project. It keeps your draft across modes, says plainly when the owner's Mac is away or needs an update, and labels teammate messages with a Teammate badge in every thread. The owner sees FROM A TEAMMATE posts in their Orchestrator thread.

Terminal calls your computers machines, not Macs: the Hand off picker reads "This machine" and "Your other machines", Settings reads "Stop all work sent to this machine" and "Run my automations on this machine", and onboarding, move and handoff messages, and the tool descriptions and results agents read say machine too. Only features that need macOS (keep awake, server mode, the automation sandbox, Apple Speech, the macOS permission rows) still say Mac. A handoff tile an older Terminal labels "This Mac" is still read as this machine.
Add the live Markdown editing engine behind the file editor. Nothing opens it yet, so there is no visible change.
A teammate's cloud-hosted Team Orchestrator project now offers Message <owner>'s agent: the message lands in that Orchestrator's inbox, labelled as from a teammate.
A window on a computer that has quit now says the computer is offline, and its dot is no longer green, instead of reading Reconnecting… forever.

Make the Markdown Rich and Read selection highlight visible in dark themes, draw it across Rich code blocks, and let Rich fill its pane so list-only documents show. Select-all now follows the active surface after clicking a mode, tab or path row, works with the terminal find bar open and in remote-machine windows, and takes a Rich code block before the document. Copying a whole Read document keeps its Markdown, and Rich no longer loses the last keystrokes on save or mode switch. High Contrast Dark's selection no longer hides selected text.

Your feed row now says when a teammate messaged your agent: "Craig Lu messaged your agent" (or "Craig Lu's agent messaged your agent"), in blue with their avatar, until you or the agent post again. A project or chat on this machine records it on its synced card, so your other machines and the web show it too.

The Terminal settings tool descriptions agents read say "this machine" for keep awake and server mode, and Remote Desktop viewing on macOS "still needs Screen Recording permission". The rest of this change marks text that is genuinely macOS-only so the "say machine" check passes.
Signing in to a machine on the edge relay now also signs its owner in to the app, so Agent mode, its badge and the cards stream work there as they do on a tunnel. Teammates see what they saw before.
Opening a running full-screen tab from the web, phone or a project's Terminal tab shows its screen instead of an empty one

A process a worker started with a scratch or worktree path in its arguments, such as a QA Postgres, no longer blocks handing its project off. If a handoff still cannot prove a process stopped, the message now names its pid and executable.

The live Markdown editor draws tables, images, code, Mermaid, front matter and task checkboxes, and adds a slash menu, a selection toolbar and writing shortcuts. It stays hidden until the Edit mode ships.
A shared computer can delete, archive and unarchive a person's own project when another of their devices asks.

Include eligible personal Server CLI installations in fleet updates, with signed CLI download/preflight, owner-safe scheduling, compatible older-target discovery, and explicit protected-install restrictions.
Keep conversation mention menus inside the visible viewport above phone keyboards and make touch rows easier to select.

Team chats are on for every organization: the feed's My feed / Team switch and its read-ahead, Following, the chat and project visibility chips and settings, Team projects, and the share-past-chats card no longer wait on an org flag.

A kickoff sent before the visibility chip's default loaded, whose response was lost, now retries as the same attempt instead of risking a second project; changing the chip before retrying still starts a new one.

The embedded CodePress web app now receives your Terminal telemetry setting, so it records interactions only when telemetry is on. The setting is now called Crash Reports and Usage Data, and a change applies after a restart.

The project Terminal tab now fits a phone or tablet the way the sidebar terminal does, and the machine's window gets its size back when you leave the tab, close the stream or put the app in the background. Live terminal streams can also ask what runs in a tab to repaint.

Terminal now signs its own tunnel calls (connector token, moving a tunnel, Secure Access, share links, and opening a computer or chat a teammate shared with you), so they keep working where an organization requires proof from a confirmed computer. A remote viewer's sign-in that the daemon forwards to mint an owner session is never signed by this computer.

A large Browser Tab preview no longer loses modules when one access check is slow: a stalled Browser Tab access check is asked again once, and a secure access status that expires mid-check is read again.

For an organization with local-first routing on, a job in the Mac sandbox that needs the network now gets a network of its own and reaches the internet and nothing else: not this Mac's services, your network or tailnet, or another job. Turning on jobs or automations installs the guard in the same macOS password dialog, Settings shows its state and why it isn't holding, and a Mac without it refuses those jobs with a reason while jobs with no network need still run. It turns on macOS's packet filter, and other apps' virtual machines lose link-local IPv6 to this Mac.

With Unified Apps turned on, the Apps page shows where each App's code lives and who hosts it, and connected repositories can be added as Apps. The flag is off by default, so nothing changes until staff turn it on.

Every file now has a status bar: Saved, line and column, selection size, indentation, encoding, line endings, language and wrap, with word count and reading time for Markdown. A short "Copied N lines" chip confirms a real copy or cut. Line endings, indentation, language and per-file wrap change from the bar, and Ln/Col opens go to line. The breadcrumb can copy the path, and the palette adds Copy path, Copy relative path and Copy link to line. The old status rows are gone, and Monaco's find widget follows the theme.
Share home-relative mention translation with web threads and carry conversation picks on synced messages and answers.
When opening a machine from its tunnel page needs a passkey press, the page now takes you to the web sign-in to press it and brings you back, instead of repeating "try again".

Intel Macs, and Apple silicon Macs on macOS 13 to 15, can now run your automations. Turning on "Run my automations on this Mac" downloads CodePress's sandbox runtime, with no password, and a job there reaches the public internet and nothing else: not this computer, your network or other jobs.
The project Terminal tab now has the sidebar terminal's quick keys and menu row, with your synced custom keys, and it keeps room for the terminal while the phone keyboard is up.
Sync project cards in their own lane so queued or slow uploads do not delay feed updates for existing cloud copies.
Agent accounts on narrow panes: the first tag sits top right, Week comes first and every row's bar starts at the same point, and the Running pill sits under the usage line.
A chat moved to the cloud now opens as the running chat wherever it is reached, with a working composer instead of a read-only copy.
Replace waiting project snapshots while preserving transcripts and move checkpoints, probe retries before resending a snapshot, and allow five minutes for snapshot uploads.

Markdown's Read view now reads like a document: a sans-serif column about 700px wide with a clear heading scale, images that load from the document's own machine, a labelled placeholder for a missing image, code blocks with a language label and Copy, heading links on hover, tables that scroll inside themselves, and an outline that follows your place. Copy Markdown copies the whole file, and switching between Read and Source keeps the same section on screen. The mode control moved into the path row, so no surface draws a separate Markdown row, and hidden Read no longer re-renders on every edit.

Before you turn on Run my automations on this machine, Settings now says that a run's internet traffic leaves from this machine's IP address, that CodePress has no record of where it goes, only what the run reports back, and that you answer for what you choose to run.
A settings save that doesn't change who may reach this computer no longer cuts off a preview that's loading.
Local builds now rebuild the Ghostty engine when the staged copy is from an older pin. Before, they kept reusing it, and the app then opened every new tab as xterm.

Hand off keeps offering Cloud after a chat or project moves to another machine: choosing it on the old machine asks the machine it now runs on to move it to the cloud, and an asleep machine leaves Cloud listed with the reason.
Upload project cloud copies compressed using the cloud's advertised size limit, preserve long upload deadlines, and clear outdated size refusals after a newer export is accepted.

Cmd/Ctrl+F now searches the Markdown document you're reading. A find bar in Read shows "3 of 12", steps with Enter and Shift+Enter, has a case toggle, and closes with Esc, returning you to the document. It searches the words on screen, highlights every match without touching the text, and scrolls to each one. With a terminal focused, Cmd/Ctrl+F still opens the terminal's bar, and a dialog keeps the key to itself. The Markdown toolbar has a find button and the command palette has Find in Document.

Edit and Delete on a queued message now work on cloud-run Orchestrator projects too. If the Orchestrator read it first, or a Codex Orchestrator already holds it, the message stays and you are told so.

A Local Chat that moved to the cloud and is handed back to one of your machines continues there in its Local Chat row, with the cloud's turns and a "Moved back from the cloud" line, instead of opening as a tab. Open chat in the Hand off dialog selects the row, and the machine it left reads "Runs on <machine>" when it went elsewhere.
Local previews now run a recipe's companion servers, so a Storybook App works on this machine.
A large preview no longer goes blank when one access check gets a gateway error from the load balancer. The check asks once more, inside the same 10 second limit.

New chats and projects always tell the cloud which visibility to use: a project started by another project takes its parent's Team or Personal, a chat promoted to a project keeps its visibility, and the Visibility control waits for the cloud's answer instead of reading a new copy as unlisted.
The kickoff composer's repository chip keeps what you picked across restarts, new windows and finished kickoffs, and its menu has a Clear all action.
Keep the new web-only Interactions page out of Terminal's shell: no rail entry and no page.

The owner of an Unlisted Orchestrator project can now make it Team or Personal from the project's ⋯ menu (Project actions on a phone). The menu says the project is not shared with your team yet, and Personal applies without asking because nobody could read it before. Projects kept Local only and chats are unchanged.

Orchestrator kickoff: Runs on now remembers your choice (Auto, This machine, Cloud, another machine or a shared computer) for each organization across restarts, reloads and sends, instead of resetting to Auto.

Any Orchestrator project can land, whatever its state. A project still being briefed or planned now has Land project… in its menu, its land ask opens once its work is done, and the Orchestrator can land it itself, so a project that shipped without pressing Build is no longer stuck.

Auto now treats a machine in your saved order as busy when its CPU and RAM use, averaged, reaches your limit, or when either one reaches 95%, instead of when either one alone reaches the limit. The Runs on menu says why Auto passed over a ranked machine, for example "89% combined, over your 85% limit" or "RAM at 96%".
Report named setup steps, with timings and download progress, while a local preview starts.
Show account-row warnings in full at narrow widths while keeping ordinary summaries compact.

Markdown files now open in Edit in place of Rich: the document stays rendered as you type, and saving changes only the lines you changed. Edit has find and replace, the outline, the status bar and place-keeping, and the outline now works in Source too.
Update the bundled Codex SDK and generated app-server protocol to 0.166.0.

Terminal no longer starts login shells over and over to look for CLIs and PATH, which returns about a core on a busy machine. A CLI you just installed is found straight away when you press Connect, and otherwise within two minutes.

Terminal now slows agents when the CPU runs hot, for everyone and without an organization flag: it limits capacity grants, paces worker launches and caps running workers while the machine is hot, including when signed out. To let agents use every core, turn off "Slow agents when the CPU runs hot" in Settings, or set `cpuThermalThrottling` to false with `update_terminal_agent_settings`; the change applies without a restart.
Apply remote Claude and Codex account picks like picks on the target machine, and preserve never-chosen subscription modes.

When the updater cannot deliver a status to a daemon, the log now names the port and what actually failed (connection refused, timed out or the HTTP status), and a repeated failure is logged once until it succeeds or the cause changes.

Keep the daemon responsive with many Computer Use tabs: on Linux, process identity comes from `/proc` with no child process, and activity checks no longer read it for tabs that cannot match. Diagnostics report event-loop delay and the worktree timing line now accounts for the whole creation.
Terminal now keeps `record-session.log`, `background-service.log` and oversized rotated logs within a size limit without a restart, and stops repeating two identical sweep messages in its logs.

Hand off → Cloud now works on a project or chat another of your machines holds while that machine is asleep or not answering: the cloud takes it from the copy saved there instead of the Cloud tile reading "Asleep". The machine stands down when it wakes and keeps aside what it did after that copy was saved.

A chat on your own machine can now work in any folder you pick, git or not, without adding it to Local checkouts first. Your home folder and the app's data folder are still excluded, and teammates on a shared machine are limited as before. In the kickoff, a machine picked under Runs on now offers its folders for Chat instead of asking for an app update, and you can browse to any folder on it.

A headless server that finished moving from the desktop app can restart again after its people opened new tabs, including teammates' sessions and closed terminal tabs. It used to exit with `adoption_topology_changed`. A damaged tab inventory, a second window with sessions, and a move that is not yet verified are still refused.

When CodePress asks this machine to stop a chat's agent so a project can be deleted, Terminal now confirms once the agent has really stopped (or was not running), so the project's deletion can finish.
Add an optional hook for a chat start refused for a passkey press to the shared chat core. Terminal doesn't set it, so its chats behave as before.

Deleting an Orchestrator project that is still starting now cleans it up: a repeat delete no longer errors, the row stops showing, a cloud copy created mid-delete is retired, and the project's session worktree is removed.

Ask who should see your older chats and projects: the card at the top of the feed and the row in Preferences now offer Make Personal and Share with team for everything that isn't shared or private yet, name the date to choose by, and show progress, the result and a Retry. An older chat's own ⋯ menu offers Team or Personal too, with "Not shared with your team yet".

A teammate's change now shows in Team, and in a followed row under Following in My feed, within seconds and without reloading the rail, as on the web. Team keeps applying changes while you look at My feed, so switching back draws them at once with no read; after more than 45 seconds away it reads Team once. Frames for another organization are ignored, and Terminal keeps its saved Team list current too.

A teammate's shared Orchestrator project keeps its composer (Start my own chat, Start my own Orchestrator project, Message <owner>'s agent) under the thread while the Work panel is open, as the owner's own composer does.
Hand off opens the project, chat or session in this window instead of sending you to another machine's window, and the picker draws the selected tile's whole border.
Sign edits to an automation, so turning one on or scheduling it from Terminal keeps its proof and it can still run on your machines.
Code files in the app have their theme, syntax colours, line numbers and selection highlight again. The app's own Content Security Policy was blocking every inline style, in installed builds only.

Projects waiting for their first cloud copy no longer deadlock or pile up queued uploads: the card that creates the copy always goes first, other uploads wait without retrying, a refused device backs off after ten minutes, and each launch shrinks an existing backlog to one current copy.

A browser on the machine running CodePress Desktop can now prove it is on that machine, so the repo App page offers Start and shows the local preview instead of "CodePress Desktop is on another machine". Design's Local choice in the web app reads the same check and is fixed too.

Show an open file in your file manager: Reveal in Finder on macOS, Show in File Explorer on Windows and Show in File Manager on Linux, from the path row, the Orchestrator Files toolbar, file tab menus and the command palette.

A machine with no Docker or Podman can start a local preview on Desktop's managed VM: its files now live in a short folder, `~/.cp-lima`, because the old path was too long for every macOS account. A first start no longer fails on elapsed time while its download is still moving, a failed VM start shows Lima's own reason, and Storage cleanup removes a VM folder once the Terminal data folder that made it is gone.

Selected tabs and other `dark:` styles now follow Terminal's own Light or Dark theme instead of this machine's OS appearance, so the feed rail's selected My feed and All stay readable when the two differ.

Storage cleanup no longer deletes a local preview VM folder by itself. Once the Terminal data folder that made it is gone, the folder is listed under Settings → Storage → Kept with its size, and only your Remove deletes it. Remove is refused while the VM is running or anything has a file open in the folder.

Remove the 20,000-character brief cap from human Chat and Project kickoff. Use a best-effort BPE token budget from available Codex runtime context metadata while preserving full text, draft recovery and kickoff replay.

A teammate's Team project or Mac chat now draws its HTML posts, and a project with plan pages has the Plans view, the plan issue and the Plan tab. Each work item shows its worker's model and status, and a landed project shows its landing summary, all read-only, the way the owner sees them.

A Synced project's or chat's published artifacts (the Orchestrator's, its workers', closed worker tabs included, or a Synced chat's) are now copied once to its cloud copy, so teammates can open them while this machine is asleep. Artifacts published before the project was Synced are sent at the next start. A Local-only project sends nothing, and an older backend leaves them waiting without an error.

Your own machines that are signed in to another CodePress account now say "Signed in to another account" instead of Offline: in Settings → Computers, in the kickoff's Runs on (where they can't be picked), and in `list_machines` (status `other_account`, with a hint). Teammates still see Offline, and Terminal no longer keeps re-checking such a machine.

New setting in Settings → System: Prepare a worktree ahead of new workflows. With it on (it's off by default), a new workflow claims a worktree that's already checked out, so it starts in seconds; when a spare doesn't fit, it gets a normal checkout.

A repository with several packages can start a local preview on Desktop's managed VM. A preview now mounts cache volumes only for the packages its frontend can install into, and only the build cache its framework uses, which also shortens the list on Docker and Podman. If a repository still has too many packages for the VM, it fails with a clear reason before any container runs, and any failed container step now shows the engine's own reason.

A teammate's Team project shows each worker's conversation on its Agent card (words and tool calls, updated at each turn end, with Full transcript), opens a cloud worker's own chat, and has an Artifacts view to list and download what the project published.
Build Terminal without the unused static and shared library outputs, and skip Vite's compressed-size report, so packaging does less work.

In the New chat kickoff, a row without a folder chip now shows the project picker's label in full whenever the row has room, and Chat mode's model chip is the same shared component the web's phone New chat draws.

Each CodePress account signed in to the app on a machine now gets its own account space: a separate data folder with its own machine ID, projects, tabs, transcripts, settings and AI logins. Signing in as another account asks first, lists the agents that will stop, then reopens the app in that account's space; nothing from one account's space is shown to or uploaded under another, and nothing uploads while signed out.

A computer that stays healthy on the edge relay can give up its Cloudflare tunnel. It reports how long it has been attached, stops cloudflared when the backend says the relay serves it, and asks for a tunnel back when the relay is withdrawn, stays down past its limit or a Browser Tab needs one.

Orchestrator Files has one header row: the path row and the Saved / Save status are gone. Markdown's modes sit in the tabs row, Open in Terminal, Reveal and Copy path are in a ⋯ menu under the full path, and Cmd/Ctrl+S saves. No status bar shows Saved any more; a touch screen gets Save while a file is dirty.
Split the native app into a Cargo workspace with a thin app crate, so a new commit, a version bump or a frontend edit no longer recompiles the app library.

A computer the edge relay released keeps its relay connection when the relay is turned down for it, and closes it only once its tunnel has connected and stayed up, so its URL stays reachable through the handoff.

Move settings paths, the settings lock, the display-awake owner and on-device dictation into their own Rust crates, so editing dictation no longer recompiles those lower layers and editing the app no longer recompiles dictation.
Wait for a private browser display's Xvfb and stdin watcher to be reaped before reporting a successful stop. Preserve private recovery files and reject when retirement cannot be established.
Remote Desktop and desktop use now build as their own native crate, so an app change no longer recompiles them. Nothing changes in how they work.

Agents and Terminal now name this machine by the name you gave it (like "128gb" or "server cli") instead of the computer's own name, in remote-kickoff refusals, teammate failure messages, handoffs, Fleet and live-browser labels, GitHub stats, the folder browser and the desktop viewer.
Upgrade the Codex SDK to 0.167.0 and refresh its app-server protocol.

A Muse agent that hits its usage limit now says so. A strip on the composer names the account and when it resets, and the agent waits on the same account and continues there at the reset. Choose **Continue on another account** on the strip to move it yourself, the same as switching in Accounts. Terminal never moves a Muse account because of a limit on its own, and agents cannot do it for you. The Orchestrator hears what happened to its Muse workers.

Moving an Orchestrator project to another machine no longer fails with "admitted after preflight" because of an old tab left behind by a worker relaunch. Each worker is now tracked by exactly one tab: a relaunch hands the worker's claim to its new tab, and Terminal tidies tabs left by older versions when it starts and before a move, without closing any of them. If an old tab still runs an agent, the move now refuses up front and names the tab, its session and the work item.

Personal and Team Grok accounts connected on CodePress now show on the Grok tab, and Add account → Grok signs a Personal or Team one in with a device code. Choose a Personal account for this computer and CodePress leases it the access token, never the refresh token: `grok` runs on it, the token is renewed while it stays chosen, and your own login comes back when you sign out, clear it or the computer is revoked. A repository rule can bind a Personal Grok account too. Team Grok accounts and xAI API keys run cloud agents only.

The Orchestrator now knows that when your organization has Google Workspace connected, it can list your Google connections through its CodePress connection and use Google for the documents, spreadsheets, decks, email drafts and events you ask for. Plans and design issues still go to GitHub.

Picking up a project from its cloud copy no longer fails when one worker cannot be restored. That worker comes across stopped, with the reason and its cloud checkpoint kept, and the Orchestrator inbox and the move dialog name it. A worker whose tree was already removed is no longer restored at all. The repository and branch are now looked up from every source the copy carries before a worker is given up on.

A local Orchestrator can now run on Grok. Pick a Grok model at kickoff or in Project settings and the Orchestrator runs on Grok Build itself (`grok agent`), on the Grok account this machine uses, with the same tools, thread, resume and account rules as Claude, Codex and Muse. Projects stuck on the old "Grok can run workers but not the Orchestrator yet" message now start.

Moving an Orchestrator project no longer refuses with "A worker message or restart is still being delivered" when the process that was delivering it is gone. Those deliveries are settled as uncertain (never sent again), a restart left pending moves its worker as stopped (or, while its tab may still run an agent, the move refuses and names that tab or says it cannot be checked from this window), and Terminal start and PM session end clear such leftovers. A delivery that is still being written is waited on for up to a minute, with "Waiting for a message to <worker> to finish…" shown in the move.

Handing off a project no longer fails because workers were updated in the background while the move was being prepared. If a worker really changes in that window (relaunched onto a new tab, branch renamed), the move prepares again by itself and only gives up after a few tries, naming just the workers that kept changing. A merge in flight or a merged pull request still settling now makes the move wait, with a line in the dialog saying what it waits on, instead of refusing.

Grok accounts now show how much of their weekly or monthly allowance is used and when it resets, on the account card and in the Orchestrator and worker pickers. When the reading is unavailable the card says "Usage unavailable" instead of 0%. Every catalog Grok model now has a price in Settings → Usage.

Moving a project to this machine no longer needs its home machine to be awake. A home that isn't connected is not asked at all, and one that stops answering partway through is replaced by a takeover from the cloud copy after 30 seconds. If no cloud copy can be used, the move says the home isn't answering and nothing moved, and offers a plain Try again.

Keep handoff recovery refusals visible across background reads, and reset the dialog when its transfer changes.
Cancel chooser waiting reads when their start attempt settles or closes, and keep late replies out of later attempts.

Handing off an Orchestrator project no longer asks you to stop a worker, close its tab or stop a process first. The handoff stops what stands in the way itself: a worker whose agent could not be confirmed, a failed worker's leftover process, a tab-less worker's own process in its worktree, a stray tab's live agent, and the agent left running in the tab of a restart whose restarting process stopped. Tabs, worktrees, uncommitted changes, branches and pull requests are kept, and the workers move as stopped. The finished dialog, the thread and the Orchestrator say "Stopped N workers to move them: …" so they can be relaunched. A process in a worktree that is not the worker's is left alone. The move refuses only when a stop fails twice, naming what could not be stopped and why.

Factory: Next per-person switch. Terminal syncs the signed-in person's staff-managed Factory: Next enrollment to `<CODEPRESS_HOME>/factory/variant.json` on sign-in and on each settings read. On `next`, Stop guidance names `qa-verifier-next` and `falsifier-next`, and `codepress factory skill --name qa-verifier|falsifier` prints the `-next` prompt when this build carries it (today's role and an advisory line otherwise). `codepress factory variant next|current|auto` overrides the machine at once; with no file the machine stays on today's factory, byte for byte.

Picking a project up from its cloud copy now finishes for large projects. It downloads only the conversations that resume, retries dropped connections and server errors, renews expired download links, and reports which download failed and why.

Settings → Members now shows who comes in through a workspace connection: a card per connected workspace, Your team with its seat count, and a From section whose roles that workspace sets. It also says when a paying workspace has no plan yet and when that puts you over your seat limit.

A project whose workers Terminal restarted itself (a usage-limit failover, a restart the person approved, a handoff's worker resume) can be handed off and taken over from its cloud copy again; its bundle is no longer refused as carrying a foreign PM reference. A handoff whose bundle every destination would refuse now fails on the home machine with the same message, before it is sent; the cloud copy still uploads and Terminal logs a warning naming what a takeover would refuse.

A Grok agent at a usage limit now says so. Its composer strip names the account, which limit ran out and when it resets, and offers Wait for reset or Continue on another account. Terminal waits on the same account and continues there at the reset; it never moves a Grok account by itself, and agents can't either.
Your own cloud chats in the Agent feed now list Hand off… in their ⋯ menu. Choosing it opens the chat with its Hand off picker already open, or says why the chat can't leave the cloud.

Picking a project up from its cloud copy relaunches only the workers that were running. Stopped, completed and failed workers arrive in that state with their worktree restored, and the pickup note names them.
Tag automatic backend requests with X-CodePress-Activity: background so staging can distinguish background traffic from user activity.
Recover Remote Desktop bitrate and resolution after congestion, ignore idle RTT noise, and add opt-in interval diagnostics.
Reconnect Desktop viewers after session expiry and short transport drops, preserving their display and granted control with bounded retries.
Negotiate H.264 High profile with capable Desktop viewers while preserving low-latency encoding and Baseline fallback.

Agents can move an Orchestrator project from any of your machines. `handoff_orchestrator_project` takes a machine name, a `list_machines` id, a target id, `this` or `cloud:<organization>`. It makes the move the Move dialog makes, finding the project's organization by itself.
